title: A star twice as far away
hook: Change distance and predict observed flux.
misconception: observed flux doubles when distance doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply flux = L/(4πd²) to compare observed flux when distance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an isotropic source of fixed luminosity in empty non-expanding space, flux = L/(4πd²). When distance doubles, observed flux becomes ¼ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model flux = L/(4πd²); scaling exponent -2. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an isotropic source of fixed luminosity in empty non-expanding space, with a nonzero initial result. If distance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on observed flux?
recall.why: Apply flux = L/(4πd²) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/9.
